en: The Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom / [The Concise Mother]
Homage to the Omniscient One.
The noble Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, while practicing the course of the profound perfection of wisdom,
beheld the five aggregates and saw that they are empty of intrinsic nature.
In this regard, Śāriputra, form is emptiness,
and emptiness itself is form.
Emptiness is not separate from form.
Form is not separate from emptiness;
whatever is form, that is emptiness,
and whatever is emptiness, that is form.
In the same way, it is with feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
Here, Śāriputra, all phenomena are characterized by emptiness; they are unarisen and unceasing, neither defiled nor pure, neither deficient nor complete.
Therefore, Śāriputra, in emptiness there is no form, no sensation, [no perception, no mental formations, and no consciousness].
There is no perception, no mental formations, and no consciousnesses.
There are no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind;
no forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, or mental objects;
and no eye-element up to and including the mind-element.

There is no ignorance and no absence of ignorance, no exhaustion of ignorance and no non-exhaustion of ignorance; and so on, up to: no aging and death and no exhaustion of aging and death; no suffering, origin, cessation, or path; no knowledge and no attainment.
And the Bodhisattva,
relying on the perfection of wisdom, dwells with no obscuration of mind;
because there is no obscuration of mind, he is fearless, has transcended all perversions, and reaches the ultimate nirvana.
All Buddhas dwelling in the three times, by relying on the perfection of wisdom, have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Therefore, one should know that the Prajñāpāramitā is the great mantra, the mantra of great knowledge, the unsurpassed mantra, the mantra equal to the unequaled, which allays all suffering because it is true and not false; this mantra has been proclaimed in the Prajñāpāramitā. It is as follows: Gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā.
Thus concludes the Heart Sutra of the Perfection of Wisdom.
